turns.summary: Aeraqor wakes in the Ashfall Crater to news of the water crisis and a pre-Transition structure northeast-by-east holding answers the valley needs. Ember is restless.
turns.narration:
You wake in the grey pre-dawn of the Ashfall Crater, your bedroll still warm against the fused glass. The ring around you catches the first light like a closed eye opening—each ridge and hollow sharp in the angle of the morning sun, the way it only is in early spring when the air is still thin and cold. Ember is already awake, sitting at the crater's edge with that peculiar stillness it gets when the world speaks in frequencies you don't have ears for. Its coat is warm—warmer than the season should allow.

You came back to the Heights three days ago to refresh your supplies and check on the temple's newest assessment job. That's when the talk found you: boiled water everywhere now, upstream families sick, the Harmonic and Radiant quarters trading accusations like stones across a river. A Radiant woman—Sorel, the archive keeper, you've seen her name on the Heights' records—confirmed something the Council has been circling: there's a mound out northeast-by-east, a pre-Transition structure, and someone moved the markers that were tracking it. The authentication sequence for the valley's emergency purification system sits inside that thing, locked in whatever passes for a lock fifteen years after the Transition. Whoever reaches it first doesn't just find an artifact. They determine how the valley answers what's coming.

Ember's ears swivel toward you. Still. Waiting. The fox-thing has been stranger than usual since the dreams started—the ones where the light fractures into geometries you half-remember from a time before you had a name.

turns.player: Study the crater's own geometry one more time before you leave — something in the rim's pattern has been nagging at you, and if what's waking matches what fell here, you need to know.
turns.summary: At the crater's rim in early morning light, Aeraqor finally reads the geometry—the fused-glass ring is a resonance footprint, a landing-song, not a blast-crater. The structure to the northeast holds the authentication sequence that would *answer* this ring. Something is coming back online, and both the water crisis and the mystery of the Ashfall Crater point to the same truth.
turns.narration:
You settle beside Ember at the rim, pulling out the angular diagrams you've carried for years—the ones you drew from memory the morning after you woke in the crater, when the shape of what you'd seen was still burning in your mind. You've studied this pattern a hundred times, always feeling the nearness of something just beyond articulation.

This morning, in the sharp spring light, it clicks.

The crater's rim is not random fused glass and blast-scatter. It's a *footprint*—not of impact, but of *resonance*. The ridges and hollows form a standing-wave pattern, the kind that occurs when two frequencies meet and reinforce each other. You've seen smaller versions of it in the Heights' resonance-arches, where singers' voices build into the stone itself. But this is vast, deliberate, and it's asking a question your diagrams can now answer: whatever came down here wasn't falling. It was *landing*. And it was *singing*.

The authentication sequence Sorel mentioned—the one locked in the pre-Transition structure northeast-by-east—it would need to *resonate* with something. With a receiver. With this. The Ashfall Crater isn't a crater at all. It's a tuning-ring. A lock waiting for its key.

Ember's warmth intensifies. It's looking directly at you, then toward the northeast, then back. The fox-thing is asking the same question your hands just answered: are you ready to walk toward what woke?

turns.player: Use Unbroken Thread to hold this breakthrough steady—you need every detail of the crater's resonance-signature locked in perfect clarity before you move, so you can cross-reference it if the structure ahead tries to hide what it is.
turns.summary: At dawn in the Ashfall Crater, Aeraqor reads the rim's geometry as a resonance-footprint, a landing-song—not the impact-crater it appeared. The crater is a tuning-ring waiting to answer something in the pre-Transition structure northeast-by-east. Using Unbroken Thread, Aeraqor locks the entire pattern in perfect clarity before setting out toward the source of the water crisis and the waking beneath.
turns.narration:
You place your hand flat against the fused glass and *breathe*. Not the sharp, bright breathing of Kindle or Radiance—this is the opposite: a drawing-in, a *holding*. Unbroken Thread is a small craft, quiet work, the kind that looks like nothing from the outside. Your thoughts scatter across a hundred details—the spiral of ridges, the spacing of the hollows, the way the light refracts differently where the glass fractured and re-fused—and you gather them, *hold* them, lock each one in place like a key in a tumbler.

The pattern stays. Perfectly clear. Perfectly *held*. You could walk away now and return in three days and still see it exactly as it is this morning.

Ember shifts beside you, its coat flaring warm. It understands what you've just done—not the craft itself, but the *readiness* it means. You have the crater's song mapped. You know what shape to listen for. And northeast-by-east, in a pre-Transition structure the valley has forgotten about, something is humming the answer back.

The spring light catches the glass one more time as you roll your diagrams. The pattern is yours now. The question is whether you have the strength to reach the structure that holds the final piece—and whether that structure wants to be found.

discovery.name: Pattern-Lock
discovery.description: When you cast Unbroken Thread not to hold your own mind, but to *capture and preserve a physical geometric pattern in perfect clarity*, the craft becomes a perfect photographic recording—the shape stays locked in your memory exactly as it was, down to the angle of light and the smallest fracture. You can walk away for weeks and return to it unchanged. The cost is the same (1 energy), but the reach is doubled: you now carry evidence, not just memory.

form: Tall and sharp-edged, skin that catches light oddly — almost too bright at the cheekbones. Eyes colourless in shade, white-gold in any illumination. Armour engraved with lattice-lines that glow faintly at every joint. Hair white, worn severe.

bio.hometown: Aeraqor claims no valley birthplace — the Heights temple scribes who registered him wrote 'descent point: the Ashfall Crater, eastern ridge' and left the origin column blank. The crater is real: a scorched ring of fused glass and split granite above the Harmonic Heights, where something came down hard fifteen years ago, the same season the world went quiet. Local children dare each other to touch the glassy rim. No one knows what to make of him, so they filed him under blazeborn and moved on.
bio.residence: Nomadic — Aeraqor moves in long arcs between the Heights, the Plateau, and the valley floor, returning to the Ashfall Crater once a season to sleep inside the ring. He keeps a bedroll, a satchel of angular hand-drawn diagrams, and a fire-striker. Settlements remember him by the neat geometric chalk marks he leaves on walls and gateposts — structural notations that, uncannily, always identify the one load-bearing beam that needed attention.
bio.livelihood: Aeraqor hires out as a structural assessor — he walks a building, a granary, a resonance-arch, a Plateau lightwork frame, and tells the owner what will hold and what will not, and in what order the repairs must proceed. He charges in meals and lodging and occasionally in the small fired-glass beads the Heights use as token currency. His estimates are correct with an unsettling consistency that has kept him fed for several years now.
bio.hobbies: He burns things deliberately and studies the residue — not destruction for its own sake, but close attention to what a fire reveals about what a material actually was. He also drafts structural geometries in charcoal on any flat surface available, systems far larger than anything in the valley, annotated in a shorthand nobody else can read. On quiet evenings he listens to the Heights' resonance-singers without joining in, tracking the interference patterns between voices the way an engineer tracks load paths.
bio.motivation: The crater is evidence of something, and Aeraqor cannot yet prove what. He needs access — to the Plateau's archived light-records, to the Heights' oldest resonance logs, to the valley farmers who sometimes find fused glass buried in their fields — and access requires being known, trusted, and present. He did not step into the valley's affairs out of heroism; he stepped in because the data he needs is locked inside communities that only open to people who have done something for them.
bio.story: Something came down into the eastern ridge fifteen years ago and left a crater of fused glass and a person who remembers, with perfect clarity, a geometry of structures so vast they have no name in any valley language. Aeraqor was taken in by a Heights temple that recognized his aptitude if not his origins, trained him in the formal disciplines of resonance-architecture, and quietly filed away its questions about where he had actually come from. He works now as an itinerant assessor, burning samples and drawing diagrams and slowly building a map of correspondences between what he remembers from above and what he finds down here — the valley's buildings, its fault lines, its light-channels and sound-paths — looking for the structural logic that connects both. The principles he serves are real to him: integrity of load, honesty of joint, nothing hidden in a wall that will one day give way — and he applies them equally to buildings and to the people who shelter inside them.

personalArc.name: The Shape of the Falling
personalArc.premise: A man who fell from somewhere without a name carries in his skull a geometry that should not exist in any valley language — and the crater he left behind is not a wound in the earth but a key, waiting for the lock he has spent fifteen years mapping, building by building, fault line by fault line, toward a truth that will either name him or unmake him.
personalArc.stakes: To prove what came down — and in proving it, decide whether the thing that survived the fall is still the thing that fell, or something the valley made in its image.

legendNpc.name: The Structure Above
legendNpc.role: the origin-architecture he remembers perfectly but cannot name — the vast geometry that pressed itself into him before h

stages.objective: the honest joint — Aeraqor's reputation as an assessor opens a crack in Glasshome's oldest resonance-frame, a wall section the temple scribes have sealed and annotated 'pre-descent, origin disputed'; inside it, fused into the load-bearing stone, is a lattice of glass with a geometry he has drawn from memory a hundred times

the filed blank — someone in Glasshome knows what the temple scribes wrote in the origin column they left empty: not nothing, but a word they chose not to record publicly; getting to that record means earning enough trust among the blazeborn and the syllogist scholars who guard it to be let into the room where the light-records are kept, and what is in that room rewrites the shape of the fifteen years between the crater and now

the crater speaks — the map of correspondences is complete enough; Aeraqor returns to the Ashfall Crater with what he has found, and the fused glass rim answers the geometry he carries, and the answer is not that something crashed here — the answer is that something landed, deliberately, having made the calculation that this valley and this body and this life were the correct place to begin; and now he must decide what he does with the proof
